newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end at record high on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end at record high on foreign demand.

text.p: Mexico's stock market closed at a record high on Tuesday, pulled up by strong foreign demand and strength in the construction sector, dealers said.
The market's main index closed 2.281 percent, or 76.58 points higher, at 3,433.75 points.
The bolsa was pulled up after rumors spread through the market that President Ernesto Zedillo could announce plans to boost growth during his annual state of the union address on Sunday.
"The market was very firm, above all with foreign buyers...," said one analyst.
"There is more and more interest in Mexico, since the perspectives for the economy look good," said Santander Investments economist Hector Chavez.
The market broke through a strong resistance point at 3.430 points, with good volume of 141.9 million shares.
There were 69 shares that increased, 24 that fell and 17 unchanged on the day.
The Mexican market was also helped by Wall Street, where the Dow Jones average rose 17.38 points to 5,711.27 points.
The construction sector rose a strong 3.87 percent.
"The construction sector pulled up everyone. At the prices that many of these were trading at a lot of people took advantage (of the low prices)," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with Bursametrica.
Among the gainers was construction company Tribasa *, up 10.46 percent, or 1.78 pesos, to 18.80 pesos.
Cement maker Tolmex B2, rose 10.17 percent, or 3.60 pesos, to 39.0 pesos.
Cemex B was up 5.32 percent or 1.65 pesos to 32.65 pesos.
Among the losers on the day was manufacturer ECKO, down 9.84 percent or six centavos to 55 centavos.
